## TL;DR
The Releases page no longer blames the wrong workflow. A failed run of an unrelated workflow (for example Adoption matrix) no longer shows as "the release workflow failed", and an out-of-sync Homebrew row reads "Updating" while the tap's own formula-update run is in progress, instead of looking failed.

## Work and rationale
`fetchCiFailure` in `src/server/distribution.ts` now queries only the configured release workflow's runs (`actions/workflows/<file>/runs`) instead of every run for the tag. A grace window after a successful release run, and the tap's formula-update workflow (`repoos-release.yml`, repository_dispatch), drive the "Updating" label; the tap run is matched by the viewed release run's time window because the tap's run list carries no version. `docs/releases.md` says which workflow the banner refers to and how the window works. Tests cover an unrelated failed run beside a successful release run, a failed release run with the right step, an out-of-sync row inside the grace window, and an unrelated tap workflow in progress leaving the row out of sync.

## Approaches tried
Filtering the repo-wide run list by workflow name, then querying the workflow's own run list; for the tap, first a repo-wide "any active run" signal (rejected: it repeats the same misattribution), then the formula-update workflow with a time window.

## Challenges and blockers
The tap's run list has no version, so matching the viewed tag is not possible without changing the tap repo; the window match was accepted and documented, with edge cases recorded as follow-ups. The first handoff failed on a missing report section.

## Key learnings
Scope every external signal to the specific workflow it belongs to. When the data lacks a key, say so and document the approximation.
